about: Resilio Versio demo clips, round 2. Each clip is a pair rendered by the project's Renderer from one dry source: BLEND fully left (the clean passthrough) and BLEND fully right (the wet), with the same gain, so the page's BLEND slider mixes them like the knob. Sources: CC0 drum samples (Karoryfer Big Rusty Drums; Versilian Studios and Karoryfer Virtuosity Drums) sequenced in code, Wurlitzer EP200 samples by Greg Sullivan (CC BY 3.0), and a siren synthesised in code. MP3 160 kbps, 48 kHz stereo; the mix at each clip's BLEND is about -20.5 to -22 LUFS, peaks at or below -1 dBTP.

clips.title: Tubby throw and sweep
clips.caption: A one-drop groove. The snare on bars 2 and 4 is thrown into the springs, then TONE rides up to the “Big Knob” and back.
clips.transcript: A reggae one-drop at 75 bpm on a vintage kit: closed hats, kick and rimshot on beat three, soft cross-stick ghosts. On the second and fourth bars the rimshot is thrown into the springs and its tail rings on. In the last two bars the reverb thins to a telephone-like splash and then warms up again.
clips.note: Drums: Big Rusty Drums by Karoryfer (CC0), sequenced in code.

clips.title: Tubby throw and sweep (kit B)
clips.caption: The same groove on a second kit, for comparison.
clips.transcript: The same one-drop groove on a modern, tighter kit.
clips.note: Drums: Virtuosity Drums by Versilian Studios and Karoryfer (CC0), sequenced in code.

clips.title: Wurlitzer in the springs
clips.caption: Slow C minor chords on a Wurlitzer, with a long, warm tail and a little tape drift.
clips.transcript: Four slow electric piano chords in C minor, each held for a bar. The reverb is soft and wide, blooming behind each chord and drifting very slightly in pitch, then rings out after the last chord.
clips.note: Wurlitzer EP200 samples by Greg Sullivan (sullivang.net), CC BY 3.0.

clips.title: The rough end
clips.caption: VALVE with DRIVE up: a dub siren tips the tank into its howl, then DECAY comes down at 10 seconds and it falls away.
clips.transcript: Three short siren blips and a rising wail. The springs catch it and keep going on their own as a rough, moving roar. At ten seconds it drops back into a normal tail and fades.
